description: Org holds the choices that differ between organizations: where images go, how they are built, signed, scanned, and what policy they must meet.

addr.description: Addr targets an existing buildkitd (e.g. tcp://buildkitd:1234) with the local buildctl instead of starting a container.

buildkit.description: BuildKit is the moby/buildkit image used for every build. Pinning it is what makes rebuilds bit-for-bit comparable across machines.

config.description: Config is a buildkitd.toml for the BuildKit container, relative to this profile: registry mirrors, plain-HTTP or insecure registries, CA certificates. Not with addr (configure that buildkitd instead).

frontend.description: Frontend is the Dockerfile frontend pinned via `# syntax=`.

go.description: Go is the default builder image for `from: go` tools.

network.description: Network is the BuildKit container's network (docker or podman run --network), e.g. host, so BuildKit reaches a registry on this machine's localhost. Not with addr.

nix.description: Nix is the image providing the nix CLI for `from: nix` tools.

nixpkgs.description: Nixpkgs is the default NixOS/nixpkgs branch for `from: nix` tools.

runtime.description: Runtime runs the BuildKit container: auto, docker, or podman.

toolbox.description: Toolbox runs fetch/extract steps on the build platform.

extends.description: Extends is a shared org profile, published with clearcutt-factory profile push (or this repository's own, by path), that this one builds on: what it sets is fixed, this profile adds what it leaves to each repository, and may tighten (never loosen) its gate and policy. Each manifest's lock pins its digest.

path.description: Path is a shared profile in this repository, relative to this profile, e.g. org/profile.yaml: for the platform repository that publishes it, so it builds on what it publishes. It is this repository's own file, so it names no signer and isn't verified; the same merge rules apply. It and the files it names must be inside the repository. Each manifest's lock pins the digest profile push would publish it at, so a lock goes stale when it changes. Set ref or path, not both.

ref.description: Ref is the shared profile, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/factory/org:1. Each manifest's lock pins the digest it resolved to, and lock --update moves it.

signer.description: Signer is who may sign the shared profile: a key, or a keyless certificate identity and issuer. It is stated here because the shared profile names every other signer; the profile is verified against it whenever it is loaded. Signers names several instead.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source). Images only: a stack names no source, so a stack signer binds with sourceRepository.

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow runs sign, e.g. https://github.com/acme/checkout.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme; it limits sourceMatchesImage.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's signatures and attestations without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

signers.description: Signers are who may sign the shared profile, any one of them, so that its signer can be rotated: list the new signer beside the old, then drop the old once every version still in use is signed by the new. Set signer or signers, not both.

items.description: VerifyIdentity is one signer: a public key, or a keyless certificate identity with its OIDC issuer. Images signed in ClearCutt Factory's reusable workflows carry the called workflow as their certificate identity, and any repository can call them, so a keyless identity should also say which repository's runs count: sourceRepository, or sourceMatchesImage (the repository the image names as its source), optionally limited to sourceRepositoryOwner. cosign checks the certificate's GitHub workflow repository against it.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source). Images only: a stack names no source, so a stack signer binds with sourceRepository.

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow runs sign, e.g. https://github.com/acme/checkout.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme; it limits sourceMatchesImage.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's signatures and attestations without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

mirrors.description: Mirrors rewrite download URL prefixes (e.g. to Artifactory, Nexus, or Pulp). Checksums still pin the content, so a mirror can't change it.

items.description: Mirror replaces the URL prefix From with To.

allowTOFU.description: AllowTOFU permits tools whose hash was recorded on first download with no publisher checksum or digest to compare against.

allowedHosts.description: AllowedHosts restricts download hosts (exact, or ".suffix" matches): tool downloads, and the repositories apk, apt, dnf, and nix fetch packages from (apk.cgr.dev for Wolfi and Chainguard).

allowedRegistries.description: AllowedRegistries restricts image references to registries or repository paths, e.g. cgr.dev/chainguard: an entry covers itself and what is below it, whole path segments only (ghcr.io/acme covers ghcr.io/acme/app, not ghcr.io/acme-evil/app).

requireOfflineBuildTools.description: RequireOfflineBuildTools runs the scripts of from: build tools with no network (RUN --network=none), so they can only use what their builder image holds.

requireSignedStacks.description: RequireSignedStacks requires stacks fetched from a registry to carry a signature from the org's stack signer: signing.stacks (else signing.verify), or the stack signers of signing.trustPolicy.

scan.description: Scan adds a syft scan to the SBOM declared from the lockfile.

key.description: Key signs images in key mode: a file (relative to this profile) or a cosign KMS URI.

mode.description: Mode is keyless (Sigstore OIDC), key (file or KMS URI), or none.

profile.description: Profile is who signs this profile when profile push publishes it, so that pushing it unchanged only moves its tag. Repositories that extend it trust the signers they name in extends, not this.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source). Images only: a stack names no source, so a stack signer binds with sourceRepository.

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow runs sign, e.g. https://github.com/acme/checkout.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme; it limits sourceMatchesImage.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's signatures and attestations without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

stackKey.description: StackKey signs stacks (stack push) in key mode instead of Key, so stacks can have a signer of their own (see Stacks).

stacks.description: Stacks is who may sign the stacks manifests here build on, for policy.requireSignedStacks. Stacks usually come from a platform repository, so they need their own signer; empty means Verify.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source). Images only: a stack names no source, so a stack signer binds with sourceRepository.

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow runs sign, e.g. https://github.com/acme/checkout.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme; it limits sourceMatchesImage.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's signatures and attestations without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

trustPolicy.description: TrustPolicy is a ClearCutt trust policy file (apiVersion clearcutt.dev/v1, kind TrustPolicy), relative to this profile, shared with clearcutt-verify. When set, its image signers replace verify and its stack signers replace stacks.

verify.description: Verify is who signs this repository's images. `verify --image`, the already-published check, and repeating rebases verify against it.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source). Images only: a stack names no source, so a stack signer binds with sourceRepository.

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow runs sign, e.g. https://github.com/acme/checkout.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme; it limits sourceMatchesImage.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's signatures and attestations without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

allowLocalVEX.description: AllowLocalVEX, in a shared profile, also applies the VEX statements of the repositories that extend it (their profile's vex and their manifests' spec.vex), which are refused otherwise: a statement that a vulnerability doesn't apply lets an image past the gate.

failOn.description: FailOn blocks push/sign at or above this severity: negligible, low, medium, high, critical. Empty never fails.

onlyFixed.description: OnlyFixed only counts vulnerabilities with a fix available toward FailOn.

vex.description: VEX are VEX documents (OpenVEX, or CSAF), relative to this profile, applied to every scan, as a manifest's spec.vex is to its own.
